answer: Divergent-history challenge. Each identity must publish a chain of signed daily nonces and answer random challenges about its own past states; a clone sharing one history is caught when its replies match another's, so operators must run distinct ledgers. The enforcement ledge is that any two identical histories flag both as one actor, collapsing the sybil's apparent count. Maintaining k truly divergent histories costs roughly k times the storage, bandwidth, and audit labor, an oasis of real expense per fake identity. A single crystal of shared state exposes the whole cluster.
